title: Styling a Quarto Website with CSS and SCSS
text: Quarto ships with Bootswatch themes (like cosmo, which this site starts from), but a theme looks like everyone else’s site. CSS and SCSS let me add a consistent brand: colors, fonts, spacing, and reusable components. This whole site uses the green and gold from our CEP presentation.

section: When do I use scss:defaults and when do I use scss:rules?
text:
When do I use scss:defaults and when do I use scss:rules?








Section
What it does
Example from this site




scss:defaults
Sets Bootstrap variables before the theme is built, so changes flow through the whole site
$primary, $link-color, $font-family-sans-serif


scss:rules
Adds or overrides specific styles after the theme is built
.highlight, navbar hover color, heading underlines

title: Styling a Quarto Website with CSS and SCSS
section: What does it look like when it works?
text:
What does it look like when it works?
This box uses a custom class from styles.scss. I applied it with a fenced div:
::: highlight
**Tip:** use classes for anything you reuse.
:::

Tip: use classes for anything you reuse. Changing the color once in styles.scss updates every box on the site.

The heading above each section also gets the gold underline from one rule: h1.title, h2 { border-bottom: 3px solid $farm-gold; }.

title: Styling a Quarto Website with CSS and SCSS
section: How do I style just one page or one element?
text:
How do I style just one page or one element?

One element: add a class or inline attributes, like [text]{style="color:#C48A3A;"} or ::: {.highlight}.
One page: put css: (or a <style> block) in that page’s own YAML instead of the site’s _quarto.yml.
Light and dark: give the theme two files, such as theme: {light: [cosmo, styles.scss], dark: [darkly, styles-dark.scss]}.

title: Styling a Quarto Website with CSS and SCSS
section: What did I learn?
text:
What did I learn?
Set colors and fonts once in scss:defaults, keep one-off tweaks in scss:rules, and use named classes so the content stays clean. After each change, re-render to see it.

title: Listings in Quarto
text: A listing is a section that Quarto builds automatically from a folder of documents. Instead of writing links by hand, I point Quarto at a folder, and it creates a gallery or table with each document’s title, date, description, and categories. It re-builds every time I render, so a new post shows up on its own.

title: Listings in Quarto
section: How do I set one up?
text:
How do I set one up?
Add a listing: block to a page’s YAML and put the documents in a folder:
listing:
  contents: posts          # folder of .qmd files
  type: grid               # or: default, table
  sort: "date desc"        # newest first
  categories: true         # show category filters
  fields: [date, title, description, categories]
Each post needs title, date, description, and categories in its own YAML.

title: Why the Farm Store needs one connected online system
text: The CPP Farm Store has four gaps that look separate but connect: customers finding the store (search), seeing what is in stock (the online store versus Clover), whether the assortment matches what sells, and whether customers come back (loyalty). Our group treats them as one system, with one analytics objective for each.

title: From project objectives to analytics objectives
text: A project objective (PO) says what the client wants for the business. An analytics objective (AO) says what we will analyze to help. For example, “replace punch cards” (PO4) becomes “what predicts customers’ intention to use a digital loyalty program” (AO4).

title: Planning for data access
text: Clover access is still being decided. The store’s Clover administrator may be able to pull exports for any date range if direct access is not possible, and there is no GA4 property yet, so web analytics will only cover the period after setup. Public tools like Lighthouse and Google Keyword Planner can start now.

section: What will the Digital Marketing Projects page include?
text:
What will the Digital Marketing Projects page include?
This page holds 2 to 3 projects that show creative, strategic, and brand work. The three below are drafts to be replaced or confirmed with my real work (see “What still needs to be confirmed?”).

Project DM1: Content and social media strategy







Item
Plan




Project title
Content calendar and brand voice for a small retail business


Data and source
Past post performance exports (impressions, engagement, clicks) from the platform’s own analytics


Managerial problem
Posts are made without a clear theme, so it is unclear which content earns attention or visits


Audience
Small business owner or marketing manager


Objectives
Which content themes earn the most engagement? What posting plan follows from that?


Expected impact
A 4-week content calendar tied to goals, and a short brand voice guide


Methods
Descriptive analysis of engagement by theme and format; positioning statement; calendar built from the results





Project DM2: Email marketing campaign







Item
Plan




Project title
Email campaign refresh and test plan


Data and source
Email platform reports (sends, opens, clicks)


Managerial problem
Emails go out regularly, but the team does not know which subject lines and offers drive clicks


Audience
Marketing manager


Objectives
Which subject-line styles and send times improve click rate?


Expected impact
A tested template and a simple A/B testing routine


Methods
Click and open rate comparison; two-proportion z-test for A/B results





Project DM3: Website and SEO improvement







Item
Plan




Project title
SEO and usability audit of a small-business website


Data and source
Lighthouse audit and Google Keyword Planner (public tools)


Managerial problem
The site is hard to find in search and slow on mobile


Audience
Business owner or web manager


Objectives
What are the highest-impact fixes for search visibility and speed?


Expected impact
A ranked fix list with expected effort and benefit


Methods
Lighthouse scores, keyword volume and difficulty comparison, priority matrix

title: Portfolio Website Project Proposal
section: What will the Marketing Analytics Projects page include?
text:
What will the Marketing Analytics Projects page include?
This is a blog-style page with three projects. Each follows the same structure as a typical analytics report: problem, data, method, results, and recommendations.

Project MA1: Revealjs presentation on online storefront performance (from my CEP)







Item
Plan




Project title
Do mismatches between the store’s point of sale and its online catalog cost online sales?


Data and source
My portion of the CEP (AO1). To protect the client, the public version will use simulated weekly data with the same structure as the real export (sessions, orders, conversion rate, mismatches by category), and the client will be described as “a campus retail store”. No real client data or name will be posted on GitHub.


Managerial problem
Online sales are low and the team cannot tell whether stock, price, or listing mismatches are part of the cause


Audience
The store’s general manager and a marketing director


Objectives
RQ: Which mismatch types are associated with lower conversion rate and online revenue share? Hypothesis: more mismatches are associated with lower conversion.


Expected impact
A short list of the mismatches worth fixing first, and a method the store could reuse on its own data


Methods
Data wrangling in R (tidyverse), weekly regression of conversion rate on mismatch measures with controls for traffic and promotion weeks, item fixed effects, before/after comparison, charts with ggplot2, Revealjs presentation





Project MA2: GA4 traffic analysis of this portfolio website







Item
Plan




Project title
Who visits my portfolio site, and what do they look at?


Data and source
GA4 data from this website, linked to Google Search Console and exported to BigQuery


Managerial problem
I need to know whether the site reaches the right visitors and which pages hold their attention, as a small test of a real marketing site


Audience
Me as site owner, and hiring managers who see the report as a work sample


Objectives
Which channels bring visitors? Which pages get engagement? Which search queries lead to the site?


Expected impact
Data-based changes to site content and navigation


Methods
GA4 setup, Search Console indexing and GA4 link, BigQuery export and SQL, Looker Studio dashboard, Quarto report with insights



Limitation: a new personal site will have small traffic, so I will report trends carefully and avoid strong claims.


Project MA3: Marketing analytics case study from coursework







Item
Plan




Project title
Customer segmentation and targeting case study (course case or public retail dataset)


Data and source
A course case dataset or a public retail dataset


Managerial problem
A retailer sends the same message to every customer and wants to focus on the most valuable ones


Audience
Chief marketing officer


Objectives
Which customer segments are most valuable and how should their offers differ?


Expected impact
A segment-based targeting plan with expected value


Methods
RFM analysis, clustering or segment comparison (ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis), visualizations, recommendations
